transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-14 10:00 UTC
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (AE), Priya Nair (SE), Jordan Blake (PM), Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Park, Nora Li, Marcus Reed

Summary: quick run-through of messaging and then two demo role-plays; focus on concise answers for pricing/latency and when to call out Dedicated/Private options.

[00:00] Alex Chen: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, uh, quick intro then we'll go into messaging pillars, competitive, then demo practice.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: sounds good, trying to tighten up my 60-second pitch.
[00:25] Priya Nair: yeah we'll call out three pillars: performance (latency/throughput), cost predictability (dedicated/reserved), and security/compliance (private, KMS, audit logs). don't let the convo get stuck on model names.
[00:40] Sofia Martinez: quick question, when a customer says "OpenAI has the best models" how do we respond?
[00:48] Jordan Blake: acknowledge model quality, then pivot to serving differentiation — e.g., predictable latency at scale, routing/fallbacks, and cost controls via batching/quantization.
[01:05] Nora Li: right but customers ask about hallucinations too, any specific lines?
[01:12] Priya Nair: say we prioritize evals tied to your prompt set, we monitor regressions, and can do rollouts/canary to detect quality slips. also mention built-in eval alerts and regression tooling.
[01:28] Marcus Reed: people also ask about running on-prem — do we say "we can do it" or defer to solutions?
[01:34] Alex Chen: yes we say yes: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations and SOC2/ISO controls. call out that Private has extra lead time and licensing.

[05:00] Priya Nair: demo checklist — quick customer problem, show request routing live, highlight latency numbers, then a cost comparison slide. avoid deep infra talk unless the SE asks for it.
[05:22] Ethan Park: for the cost slide, are we comfortable quoting per-token numbers in a sales call?
[05:28] Jordan Blake: quote ranges; exact pricing goes to procurement follow-up. emphasize unit economics improvements (batching, caching) not raw cents.

Role-play 1 - Liam as AE, Priya as SE (live demo):
[10:00] Liam O'Connor (AE): Hi I'm Liam from Redwood Inference, quick question about your current LLM deployment, what's the main pain point?
[10:10] Customer (Sofia acting): -- Our latency spikes during peak periods and cloud costs are unpredictable --
[10:18] Liam O'Connor: got it, two levers we use are Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and automatic KV caching to reduce per-token compute; Priya, can you show a quick example?
[10:28] Priya Nair: sure, I'll demo a route that falls back to a smaller quantized model during spikes while preserving key-context via KV cache.
[10:38] [screen share simulated] Priya Nair: here you can see live request routing policy; this is a canary to a q4_8bit variant, latency drops from ~220ms to ~120ms on average, cost per token goes down ~40% in our benchmark.
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: nice, and if they say they care about accuracy?
[11:12] Priya Nair: we can show A/B quality side-by-side, and we recommend canarying quantized variants with small traffic to validate no quality regressions.
[11:30] Jordan Blake: call out the tradeoffs: quantization helps cost/latency but may need evals; that's where Redwood Optimize recommends profiles.

[20:00] Feedback round:
[20:05] Sofia Martinez: good flow, Liam should shorten the setup; go to the pain point faster.
[20:12] Ethan Park: the line about "cost per token goes down ~40%" felt too precise, maybe say "up to ~40% in similar workloads".
[20:25] Priya Nair: agree, add a qualifier. Also, include a quick line for security: "we can integrate with your KMS and preserve key custody".

Role-play 2 - Sofia as AE, Priya SE (demo with objection handling):
[30:00] Sofia Martinez (AE): many customers ask "why not just use OpenAI hosted?"
[30:08] Priya Nair: acknowledge: OpenAI has strong models, then we pivot: if you need predictable SLA, enterprise routing, private deployments or better unit economics at scale, Redwood gives hosting + dedicated + private with a unified API.
[30:25] Sofia Martinez: customer presses on model latency.
[30:30] Priya Nair: show sample latency dashboard: token-level latencies, per-route SLOs, and the ability to route by region or cost tier. mention autoscaling and burst capacity for traffic spikes.
[31:00] Liam O'Connor: what about regulatory regions?
[31:05] Priya Nair: say we offer region pinning and private deployments; for regulated workloads we recommend Private with customer-managed networking and audit logs.

[40:00] Coaching notes:
[40:05] Jordan Blake: key messaging bullets for pitch deck: 1) predictable performance, 2) flexible deployment modes, 3) cost controls + Optimize, 4) enterprise security. Keep each bullet to one sentence.
[40:30] Alex Chen: call out examples: "Customer X saved 35% on per-token cost using caching + batching" — don't invent customer names, use anonymized references.

[50:00] Open Q&A and wrap:
[50:05] Nora Li: should we call out GPU/instance types?
[50:10] Priya Nair: only if asked, otherwise it's noise. if an SE or infra buyer is present, bring up kernel selection and quantization.
[50:28] Marcus Reed: can we get a one-pager of objection responses?
[50:32] Alex Chen: yes I'll put together a cheat sheet with top 10 objections and suggested responses.

[59:00] Alex Chen: recap — Priya updates the demo script, Alex drafts the one-pager, Jordan provides benchmark slides; follow-up role-play next week. thanks everyone.
[59:20] All: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and filler words removed for brevity; rough timestamps approximate.
